Definition: a loan; by implication, interest on a debt
BiblicalUsage: mashshâʼ is a loan, and by implication the interest on a debt. In Nehemiah 5:7 Nehemiah rebukes the nobles and rulers, saying they exact usury, every one of his brother, and in Nehemiah 5:10 he confesses that he and his brethren and his servants might exact money and corn, and pleads that they leave off this usury. The word is the debt that grows on a brother.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashshâʼ shows me that charging interest to a brother in need is oppression, and I hold that Nehemiah's rebuke still stands.
